_comment: Per-shot prompt text for keyframes generated FROM THE WORLD (depth-conditioned). Layout is carried by the depth pass, so the text only has to say what things are made of, who is in frame, the weather and the look. Invariants stay POSITIVE and COUNTED (NH-USA-051).

shared.look: prestige political drama, House of Cards season one color grade, anamorphic cinematography, Arri Alexa, slight 35mm film grain, color palette desaturated twelve percent, warm tungstens lifted, deep browns and charcoals in shadows, photographic realism, cinematic
shared.gloom: a heavy flat sheet-cake grey overcast, no sun, no cast shadows, a light drizzle falling, the granite setts wet and dully reflective with shallow puddles, timber darkened where wet, street lamps and the building's windows glowing warm and doubled in the wet
shared.dress: a limestone neoclassical City Hall with a semicircular colonnade of tall columns under a drum and cupola, a mauve banner with pale lettering hanging between the columns, corn-stalk sheaves tied to the columns and lampposts, pumpkins and gourds at the column bases, garlands of autumn leaves on the balustrade, parked cars along the kerbs, a lumber flatbed truck and a white box van, a few distant pedestrians under umbrellas with their backs to us

SH003.text: Low angle from the wet paving in front of a rally stage under construction, looking straight at City Hall, square to its facade. The platform is a frame of open raw-pine joists with no decking yet; its long near edge runs perfectly horizontal across the lower third of the frame. Exactly two tall square pine uprights stand at the two ends of the platform, one at the far left end and one at the far right end, and no crossbeam. Three workmen in wet high-visibility vests and knit caps, seen from behind and in profile, steady the right-hand upright hand over hand while one holds a temporary diagonal prop; their breath steams in the cold.

SH006.text: High point of view from a tall window of City Hall looking down and out across the square, the sides of the window embrasure dark at both edges of the frame. Below, the rally stage runs perfectly horizontal, parallel to the facade: decking boards laid across the left half of the platform, the right half still a frame of open pine joists with the wet paving visible between them, a workman kneeling at the boundary fixing a board. Exactly two tall square pine uprights stand at the two ends of the platform with no crossbeam. Beyond the square a wet street with slow traffic, headlights on, a row of brick and stone shopfronts under the grey sky.

SH009.text: Head-height medium shot from the wet paving in front of the left end of the finished rally stage, looking straight at City Hall, square to its facade. The stage's long near edge runs perfectly horizontal across the frame; its left end with a short flight of four raw-pine steps sits right of centre; exactly one row of folding chairs and a podium stand on the wet decking. Exactly two tall square pine uprights stand at the two ends of the stage, the near one at the left end rising just right of frame centre, with a solid crossbeam across their tops, both wrapped in garlands of autumn leaves; pumpkins, gourds and hay bales along the stage front and beside the steps. A single workman in a wet high-visibility vest, in profile, puts his weight on the first tread of the steps to test it, one hand on the platform edge.
